It might be a long time until machine intelligence reaches the point where computers can write better stories and create better paintings than humans can. Creativity isn't even understood in humans yet. However, we have already reached the point where machines are better than humans at an incredible number of physical and mental tasks. You have no hope of ever welding a car's frame or inputting data into a spreadsheet as accurately or fast as a robot can. So the future I see coming is one in which the only tasks left to humans are ones requiring creativity, because creativity is really the only arena left in which humans are still far superior in their ability compared to machines.

So what would the economy and government of that world look like? How will people earn money, exchange goods, participate in commerce, etc. when maybe only 1% of the population at most needs to be employed? In our current society, things need to get done by people, so we incentivize people to do those things by offering them money. If everything is done by a robot, people don't need to get things done anymore, so we don't need to creative incentives for them to work. How will we motivate people (and why would we want to or need to?) in this hypothetical future?

TLDR: How will billions of people spend their time in a future that doesn't require them to work?
What will people do in a world where all forms of non-creative physical and mental labor can be performed by robots?
